items.headline: The AI trade splits: hyperscalers rally while neoclouds sell off
items.summary: On Wednesday, Amazon and Microsoft each jumped about 7% and Google about 4%, while CoreWeave fell nearly 10%, IREN about 11%, and Nebius about 6–7%. Commentators on X read the move as a bet that data-center pushback and local delays will hit pure-play neoclouds harder than the big cloud platforms, consolidating the market toward the hyperscalers. Separately, Oguz Erkan argued semiconductor valuations have already peaked relative to margins, with the easy money in chips largely made and demand expected to ease after 2027.
items.short: AMZN/MSFT ~+7% vs CRWV/IREN/NBIS down hard; market prices neoclouds as more exposed to data-center delays.

items.headline: Micron scraps a planned Taiwan fab; less memory supply for 2028
items.summary: Jukan reported that Micron scrapped plans for another Taiwan fab that was supposed to come online in 2028, after the local union pushed for higher bonuses — implying less supply hitting the market that year. Paradis noted Micron's Taiwan bonuses were about 4–5% of operating income versus roughly 10% at SK Hynix and Samsung, calling the gap ludicrous given Micron's recent operating income.
items.short: Micron cancels a 2028 Taiwan fab amid bonus dispute; less HBM/DRAM supply later this decade.

items.author: Andrej Karpathy
items.text:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.author: GREG ISENBERG
items.text:
running a company nowadays feels kinda dystopian

my team is 50+ people in 12 countries, but i talk to my agents more than my human teammates

- voice note to grokbot
- mattpocock/skills /grill-me so the agent interrogates the idea before anything gets built
- spec drops into linear through the linear mcp
- exa + firecrawl agent reads every competitor site, pricing page and changelog
- https://t.co/a5ARFnvSnA to find ideas and trends
- apify pulls g2, reddit and app store reviews
- prompt: "find the 10 complaints that show up most and quote the users"
- context7 so the agent reads the latest docs before it touches any api

the design

- claude code + paper mcp
- 4 versions of every screen before a single line of code
- pick pieces from 2, it merges them. diverge then converge
- frontend-design skill from anthropic/skills + our own design system skill
- cleanshot screenshots of any ui i like go straight in with "make it feel like this"

the build

- pingdotgg/t3code as the control surface for every agent, from my phone too
- stablyai/orca runs a fleet of agents in parallel, each in its own git worktree
- graphify maps the whole codebase into a knowledge graph so agents navigate instead of guess
- headroom compresses tool outputs before they hit the model, so tokens go 20-95% further
- lsp plugins so the agent sees types and errors like an ide does
- security guidance hook flags risky edits before they land
- supabase mcp for the database, stripe for billing
- github mcp opens the pr, vercel spins up a preview
- loops run overnight, i check what shipped over coffee

the user testing

- lightpanda as the headless browser, way lighter than chromium so you can run hundreds at once
- agents click every flow on the preview like a first-time user
- one persona is impatient, one is confused, one is on a phone
- playwright + chrome devtools mcp for regression tests

the bugs

- sentry mcp catches the error
- agent reads the stack trace and opens a fix pr in under 10 minutes
- human just approves

the data

- posthog mcp cron at 7am on yesterday's funnel
- any step that drops more than 10%, the agent watches 20 session replays and tells me why
- stripe mcp pulls every cancellation reason into one doc every monday

the agents' tools

- orgo so every agent gets its own computer
- agentmail so every agent gets its own inbox
- agentphone so i can call them from the car
- composio connect-apps for every other connector
- akitaonrails/ai-memory, a git-backed markdown wiki so they remember what we decided last week

the skills

- wshobson/agents so skills work across claude code, codex and opencode
- my writing voice
- our design system
- how we write specs
- skill creator so the agents write new skills themselves

some helpful tricks

- one agent per platform. the x agent never touches email
- cheap model for triage, opus for anything that ships
- every output gets scored 1-10 by an llm judge. under 8 goes back
- every agent writes a 5-line log at night so i can read the whole company in 2 minutes
- every agent mistake becomes a new skill, so it only happens once

the team

- humans get version 5, not my voice note which they are happy about lol 
- their job is creative feedback, relationships and telling the agents what they got wrong

a human pm reviews the funnel once a week. this reviews it every morning

running a company is now voice notes and inference

2027 Is going to be an absolutely wild year for knowledge work 

I actually think there will be far more opportunity in terms of jobs, but you are going to have to work with agentic coding models. It's still early so a lot of stuff isn't abstracted away 

I have had a surprising amount of people reach out to me in the last 2 months, wanting to just talk with somebody who's gone through letting go of a fancy work identity

The good news is that many people get to a spot where they feel happier about work.  Does that mean a guaranteed path to always making money in a very stable and secure way? No. But it does mean there are far more ways to work in today's world and be satisfied with that 

I think the key is to not trade your present for the future. Fear and worry. And the sense that you are "behind," are always stealing your present. And the present is the only way you can actually channel curiosity or creativity - the best way to embrace an emergent path

items.author: Daniel Koss
items.text:
Short $NBIS, long $ORCL.

This Citrini trade seems absolutely INSANE to me. 

The exact OPPOSITE trade seems much smarter.

1) COUNTERPARTY RISK: Oracle's largest customer is OpenAI (~$300B deal). Oracle is BBB-, one notch above junk, with ~$118B of long-term debt. Nebius's backlog sits on investment-grade Microsoft and Meta contracts and is financed against them.

2) Execution risk: Oracle had reported OpenAI site delays and a slower Abilene ramp. Nebius delivered every Microsoft and Meta tranche on time.

3) Regulatory risk: Oracle's Stargate footprint is heavily in TEXAS, the exact moratorium risk Citrini warns about. Nebius has ZERO disclosed Texas sites.

4) Geographic flexibility: Nebius builds across Europe, the Middle East (Israel, NEOM) and is expanding into APAC.

No matter which angle you look from, this pair is the exact opposite of what you'd do for every reason Citrini seems to fear. Just makes no sense 🤷‍♂️

items.author: Oguz Erkan
items.text:
We are likely near the peak of the AI cycle.

Historically, semiconductor valuations peak just before margins peak, which indicates a turning point in the cycle.

Forward multiples have been contracting this year while margins have kept expanding. Given that multiples roll over before margins, we’ll likely see peak margins next year.

This means demand is expected to ease post-2027.

So, the easy money in semiconductors has already been made. There could still be some upside to $NVDA and $AMD, depending on how fast demand cools post-2027, but nobody should expect the violent upward moves we saw in the last 2–3 years.

items.text:
Scott Kupor (@skupor) was the first hire at Andreessen Horowitz. Marc and Ben still joke that if he had said yes sooner, the firm would be called Andreessen, Kupor, Horowitz.

His job description: "We're going to invest, and you need to figure out everything else."

items.title: Four Cards
items.rule: If a card has a vowel on one side, it has an even number on the other.
items.explanation: A could hide something that breaks the rule; 9 breaks it if the other side turns out to be A. 2 can't break it (the rule never says only those cards have it), and R isn't covered by the rule at all. Most people pick the card that matches the rule's second half instead of the one that could falsify it.

items.author: a16z
items.text:
Top-quartile venture beat top-quartile buyout through the internet buildout and again through mobile and cloud, and a16z's Jen Kha argues we're at the start of the next wave.

Tech buyouts have long been the "safe" bet in private markets. Now the stress is showing:

- In the first half of 2026, venture funds marked their tech holdings up 16%, while buyout funds marked theirs down 4%

- 70% of the debt foreclosed in 2025 and 2026 came from deals done in 2021 or 2022

- A typical buyout now needs 10 to 12% EBITDA growth a year to make 2.5x in five years, up from about 5% in 2015 …
